body: Greenland's coverage is split into over fifty disjointed parts. This guide is structured into land coverage and boat coverage sections, focusing on locations with distinctive features.
All coverage in Greenland was captured with a Generation 3 trekker camera, which was often attached to a variety of vehicles.
Most locations have their own unique Street View vehicles, such as a red tractor or a snowmobile with a large box at the front.
Greenlandic architecture consists of small, colourful wooden houses that are often sparsely placed. Major cities have larger, more minimalistic buildings.
The Greenlandic landscape is very barren, with no trees and often featuring snow. Mountains and hills are common, and since most coverage is coastal, fjords are a frequent sight.
Boat trekkers are very common in Greenland and feature a variety of different boats.
Nuuk is most easily recognized by the grey Street View car and by being the largest city by far.
Sisimiut can be recognized by the black snowmobile with side mirrors pointing straight up. The coverage is generally very overcast and grey.
Ilulissat is recognized by a green ATV with a driver wearing a beige hat. The coverage is fairly sunny and bright.
Qaqortoq can be recognized by the red rectangular car. The coverage is extremely sunny and the area is greener than most of the country.
Aasiaat is recognizable by a shiny red, white, and black reflection on the windshield. The coverage is very sunny with thick, thawing snow.
Tasiilaq can be recognized by an ATV with large grey handguards. The coverage has many thin clouds and the area is somewhat green.
Uummannaq has two distinctive features: a sharp mountain to the north and a green snowmobile with large black side mirrors.
Narsaq can be identified by the thin antenna seen on the right side of the car. The coverage is very sunny and fairly green.
The coverage in Maniitsoq was taken by a tractor, making it very recognizable. The coverage is overcast and fairly snowy.
Narsarsuaq can be recognized by the driver wearing a black hoodie. The coverage, taken near sunset, features an unusual amount of small bushes.
Across the fjord from Narsarsuaq, a black ATV with an orange and purple bag in the front can be seen. This area has tall green grass and unusually red dirt.
Qeqertarsuaq is most easily recognized by the blue ATV with wide side mirrors. The coverage is fairly overcast with a lot of yellow grass.
Ittoqqortoormiit can be recognized by the brown wooden box at the front of the ATV and the driver wearing a purple beanie. The ground is mostly grey and stony.
Igaliku is most easily recognized by the wide, snow-covered mountain range to the northeast, which looks very bright due to the setting sun. A green ATV is also present.
Paamiut can be recognized by the round, grey car which is often only barely visible. The foliage consists of a mixture of yellow and green grass, and reddish moss.
Kangerlussuaq can be recognized by the many streaky clouds in the sky, combined with significant dryness. The roads have an unconventional look, with many small bushes and sandy soil.
The road east of Kangerlussuaq is easily recognized by the large white truck.
The road between Sisimiut and Kangerlussuaq is recognized by the thick layer of snow. The sun sets along the road, making western parts bright and eastern parts dark.
North of Saattut, a wide mountain range shrouded in clouds is visible. The area has dark, muddy dirt roads and yellow grass tufts.
Kulusuk island features a round, red ATV, with a pyramid-shaped mountain often visible to the northeast. The coverage is fairly dark, taken right after sunset.
Kangaatsiaq has a large amount of thawing snow on the side of the roads. The sun is setting and there is a large body of water to the west.
Ikerasak is most easily recognized by the large monolithic mountain to the west.
Ukkusissat is located below a tall cliffside to the east with mountains towering above it.
Kuummiit can be recognized by two distinct mountains, a sharp one to the east and a rounder one to the north. The coverage is slightly dark due to clouds and the setting sun.
The houses in Tiilerilaaq are commonly grey rather than colourful. The ground is almost entirely made up of smooth, light grey rocks.
Niaqornat can be recognized by the large, dark grey rocks towering over the village.
Siorapaluk is recognized by the sandy, pyramid-shaped mountains to the north and the wide sand beach below the village.
A red and black ATV can be found in and around the village of Kapisillit, northeast of Nuuk. Many mountains in the distance are covered in a layer of snow.
Kangerluk can be recognized by the evenly tall mountains with a particular shape on the other side of the fjord.

On a small bit of coverage east of Nuuk you can see a large number of sharp mountains, powdered in snow. The coverage is somewhat dark due to the thick clouds and the sun being hidden behind the mountains.
About 20 km northeast of Narsarsuaq, you can find a small piece of coverage with large ice blocks in every direction.
In Upernavik, the airport runway is covered on Street View, making it by far the widest paved road found on Street View in Greenland.
This boat, with a white cabin and a red roof, can be found by a multitude of towns and villages on the west coast. However, most of the coverage is in the general area around the city of Aasiaat.
Similar to the previous boat, this one with a red square cabin can be found at multiple locations on the west coast, most significantly by and around Akunnaaq.

A boat with a black box near the front, and a chequered pattern on the bow can be found fairly north on the east coast. While the western part of the coverage is very foggy and somewhat overcast, the eastern parts of the coverage is slightly less foggy and very sunny. A man wearing a black coat can also be seen captaining the boat.

This bright red boat can be found on the east coast near the towns of Tiilerillaq and Kuummiit respectively. While the coverage near Tiilerillaq does not have a cloud in sight, the coverage near Kuummiit is somewhat overcast.
A black and white boat, with a blue roof, is found between the towns of Kuummiit and Tasiilaq.
This small white boat, with a brown wooden top and lights and monitoring devices, can be seen between Tiilerilaaq and Tasiilaq.
A small, rounded red bow can be found on a boat going south of Tasiilaq.
This small, red and black boat, with multiple people sitting in it, can be found in a fjord far north on the east coast.
This wooden fishing boat is found outside Ilulissat.

This small, white boat with a silver handrail on the bow can be found west of Narsaq and east of Qaqortoq. While the sun is in the west on the coverage near Narsaq, it is in the east on the coverage near Qaqortoq.
This large, all white boat can be seen in between Narsarsuaq with the opposing shore.
A grey boat is found east of Nuuk.
A mostly white boat, with extremely tall antennas on the rear can be found going into the fjord east of Nuuk.
